subject: profit-break-even
title: Break-Even: The First Number Investors Ask For
summary: Contribution margin, break-even units, and pricing for a small golf business.

cards.title: A golf ball business
cards.text: Say you start a business selling cleaned, sorted used golf balls by the dozen. How many dozen do you need to sell before you stop losing money?

cards.title: Fixed vs. variable
cards.text: Fixed costs don't change with how much you sell, like a $90 cleaning setup and a $30 website for the season. Variable costs rise with each sale, like buying used balls and egg cartons.
cards.example: In this example: fixed costs = $120. Each dozen costs you $6 in balls and packaging.

cards.title: Contribution margin
cards.text: Contribution margin is what each sale contributes toward fixed costs: price minus variable cost. Sell a dozen for $14 with $6 of variable cost, and each dozen contributes $8.

cards.title: The SBA formula
cards.text: Break-even units = fixed costs ÷ (price − variable cost per unit). Here: $120 ÷ ($14 − $6) = 15 dozen. Dozen number 16 is your first real profit.
cards.example: The SBA suggests adding about 10% for costs you can't predict, so plan on about $132 of fixed costs, or 17 dozen.

cards.title: Why investors care
cards.text: The SBA notes investors want to know not just the return they can expect but when they will see it. Many businesses lose money for months or years before breaking even. A clear break-even point shows you understand your costs.

cards.question: You could charge $20 a dozen and break even after only 9 dozen. What might you give up by raising the price? How would you find out?
nudges: Who are your customers and what are their alternatives?
What small test could tell you which price works?

questions.q: Fixed costs $120, price $14, variable cost $6. Break-even?

options.why: That divides by the price ($14), not the contribution margin ($8).
That divides by $6, the variable cost. Use price minus variable cost.

questions.q: What is contribution margin per unit?

options.text: Price minus variable cost per unit
options.why: Right. It is what each sale contributes to covering fixed costs.
Revenue includes the part that pays variable costs.

questions.q: Which is a fixed cost for the golf ball business?

options.why: Yes. It stays the same no matter how many dozen you sell.
That rises with each sale. It is variable.
More sales need more balls. Variable.

cards.prompt: Explain this to someone at dinner in 3 sentences.

sources.title: Break-even point
sources.supports: Break-even is where total cost equals total revenue; fixed costs ÷ (price − variable cost) = break-even units; contribution margin; fixed vs. variable costs; adding about 10% for unexpected expenses; why investors and lenders ask for it.
